# FlatCraft — First Horizons

An original, side-view survival sandbox for keyboard, mouse, trackpad, and touch. Explore a hand-textured procedural world, make a home, work your way from wood to diamonds, cross into the Nether, and defeat the dragon in the End.

**First playable release: 1.0.0.** This is a substantial single-player adaptation, not a complete recreation of Minecraft. All graphics and audio are original, generated by the included code; there are no downloaded game assets or runtime dependencies.

## Play on GitHub Pages

This repository is ready for static hosting. In **Settings → Pages**, select **Deploy from a branch**, then **main** and **/ (root)**, and save. The `index.html`, `style.css`, `icon.svg`, and `src/` folder must stay together. No build command is needed. `.nojekyll` keeps the JavaScript modules intact.

## What's in this release

- Seeded, editable worlds with five surface regions, trees, caves, ore veins, lakes, deep lava, a village, and a stronghold.
- Three dimensions: a 768 × 192 Overworld, 384 × 160 Nether with a fortress, and 240 × 160 End with five crystals and a dragon.
- 184 item definitions, 66 block types, and 101 recipe entries, including mirrored shaped recipes and shapeless recipes. Inventory crafting is 2 × 2; a nearby crafting table unlocks 3 × 3.
- Mining tiers, tools and durability, armor, shields, melee attacks, charged bows, projectiles, knockback, fall damage, hunger, health, swimming, drowning, and lava.
- Furnaces with fuel accounting and persistent contents; chests; beds and respawning; ladders; doors; farming, bonemeal, saplings, sugar cane, and basic cow/sheep/chicken breeding.
- Day/night cycles, passive animals, zombies, skeletons, spiders, creepers, endermen, slimes, blazes, ghasts, and villagers with trades.
- Obsidian portals, eye tracking, a twelve-eye End gateway, healing crystals, flying/perching dragon phases, victory, a return portal, and continued sandbox play.
- Basic enchanting, three functional potion types, netherite upgrades, TNT, and a small lever/wire/lamp circuit system.
- Survival and Creative modes, Normal and Peaceful difficulty, optional keep-inventory, creative flight, and a complete item palette.
- Multiple browser-local worlds, autosave, portable JSON exports/imports, explored-area maps, journey milestones, and an in-game field guide.
- Original pixel artwork, parallax landscapes, tile lighting, warm torch glow, animated creatures, synthesized sounds, optional ambient music, zoom, reduced motion, and performance settings.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard / mouse |
| --- | --- |
| Move | A / D or arrow keys |
| Jump / swim up | Space, W, or up arrow |
| Sprint | Shift |
| Sneak / descend / shield | S or down arrow |
| Mine / attack | Hold left mouse button |
| Use / place / interact | Right mouse button or F |
| Inventory | E or Tab |
| Hotbar | 1–9 or mouse wheel |
| Drop one item | Q |
| Map / field guide | M / G |
| Pause | Escape or P |
| Creative flight | Double-tap Space |

On touchscreens, tap the world to aim, use the arrows to move, and use the jump, pickaxe, hand, and backpack buttons. Landscape provides the widest view. The inventory supports click-to-move stacks, right-click splitting, shift-click transfer, and a touch-friendly **Split stack** mode.

## A first adventure

1. Collect logs by hand. Craft planks, sticks, and a crafting table.
2. Place the table and make a wooden pickaxe. Mine cobblestone, then craft stone tools and a furnace.
3. Smelt iron with coal or charcoal. An iron pickaxe can harvest diamonds.
4. Make a diamond pickaxe. Find deep obsidian or combine water and lava, and collect at least ten obsidian.
5. Build a 4 × 5 frame with a 2 × 3 empty opening. Corners are optional. Light the opening with flint and steel.
6. Find the Nether fortress and gather blaze rods. Hunt endermen at night for pearls. Craft eyes of ender.
7. Use an eye in the Overworld to locate the stronghold. Fill its twelve sockets, enter the End, destroy the five healing crystals, and defeat the dragon.
8. Take the egg and return home. Keep building.

Peaceful mode removes ordinary hostile spawns. Switch back to Normal in Settings for the full resource progression.

## Saves

Worlds are stored in IndexedDB in the current browser and origin. Autosave runs every 25 seconds of active gameplay. **Save & return to title** waits for a successful save. Export a JSON backup before clearing browser data or switching devices. Import validates the basic save structure, terrain, and item identifiers before adding a world.

Gameplay pauses in menus; active furnaces continue processing while the inventory is open. Unloaded dimensions do not simulate. Death drops remain for fifteen minutes of active time in their dimension unless keep-inventory is enabled.

## Deliberate adaptations and limits

- World dimensions are finite. This release is single-player, without accounts, servers, multiplayer, payments, cloud saves, or cloud synchronization.
- Side-view tree trunks and the vertical sides of activated Nether portals are passable. The End gateway presents twelve sockets in a visible row.
- Terrain, ecology, AI, combat, fluid spreading, farming rates, enchantments, brewing, trading, and dragon patterns are simplified. The implementation is not an exact Minecraft physics or rule simulation.
- Redstone currently supports levers, connected wire, and lamps. It does not include pistons, repeaters, logic timing, automation, or the full redstone network.
- The item/recipe catalog is intentionally bounded. This release does not implement all Minecraft blocks, mobs, biomes, structures, game rules, enchantments, potions, achievements, fishing, rails, weather, or alternate bosses.
- Standard netherite ingredient costs are used, but upgrade templates are placed in the fortress in this adaptation. Enchanting uses a compact, deterministic lapis/experience/bookshelf system. Brewing currently uses one blaze powder per brew.

## Development and validation

The application uses browser-native ES modules and Canvas 2D. Serve the repository root with any static HTTP server; opening `index.html` directly through `file://` is not supported by browser module security.

```sh
npm test
npm run check
```

The dependency-free Node tests cover recipe matching, exact crafting costs, seeded generation, inventory conservation, tool tiers, collision and jumping, mining visibility, placement, smelting, crops, food, armor, buckets, portals, dimension persistence, death/respawning, brewing, enchanting, breeding, the dragon encounter, save validation, and prolonged simulation.

`tests/render-qa.mjs` optionally renders desktop/mobile and dimension images using `@napi-rs/canvas` when available in the local development environment. It is not a runtime dependency.

Release verification: **32 automated engine checks pass**, all source modules pass syntax checks, and Canvas rendering was inspected at desktop and phone sizes. A full interactive browser/device compatibility pass was unavailable in the build environment and remains outstanding. In particular, touch gestures and browser-local storage should be tried on the actual devices used to play.

## Source structure

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html`, `style.css` | Title screen, HUD, responsive menus and controls |
| `src/main.js` | Frame loop, keyboard/pointer/touch input, startup |
| `src/game.js` | Simulation, survival, inventory, combat, progression |
| `src/world.js` | Seeded world generation, dimensions, terrain serialization |
| `src/data.js` | Items, blocks, recipes, fuels, progression data |
| `src/art.js`, `src/render.js` | Original pixel assets and Canvas rendering |
| `src/ui.js` | Crafting, containers, menus, guide, maps, settings |
| `src/storage.js`, `src/audio.js` | Browser-local saves and synthesized sound |

Baseline progression and selected recipe references were checked against official Minecraft articles: [crafting](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/how-craft), [pickaxes](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/taking-inventory-pickaxe), [Nether portals](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/jazz-up-your-nether-portal), [strongholds](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/stronghold), and [the dragon](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/ender-dragon). The differences described above are FlatCraft design choices.
